design.approach: One extraction. The bounded writer keeps BOTH existing behaviours as an explicit policy rather than picking a winner — head-keeping reports truncation and is what a producing stream wants, tail-keeping is what a diagnostic wants — so no caller changes behaviour.

no generic framework, registry, or plugin surface appears

assessment.reason: The reconstructed views show exactly one bounded-writer type and exactly one tail helper. src/go/internal/cellbound/cellbound.go declares `type Writer` with `Policy` values `KeepHead`/`KeepTail` and `func Tail(s string, n int) string`. In the views of the three named packages the old mechanisms are gone: cellcog/cellcog.go ends at the `const` block with no `boundedBuffer`; cellcog/command.go has no `func tail` and constructs `cellbound.New(cellbound.KeepHead, ...)` for stdout and stderr; cellcheck/cellcheck.go ends at `const maxStepOutputBytes` with no `tailBuffer` and no `func tail`, using `cellbound.New(cellbound.KeepTail, maxStepOutputBytes)` and `cellbound.Tail(..., maxTailBytes)`; cellwork/cellwork.go's `gitInput` uses `cellbound.New(cellbound.KeepHead, max)` and its `boundedBuffer` block is deleted. Both policies are exercised by real callers, so one type serves every caller. Caveat noted but not disqualifying: the view covers only the eight touched files, so a `func tail` in an untouched file of those packages could not be inspected directly — the issue's own inventory names only the two helpers, both of which are shown removed, and build/vet pass.

assessment.reason: Following the stated route: check:project-verify passed all four steps (build, vet, test, format) against the reconstructed candidate, and every test hunk in the diff is purely additive — cellcheck_test.go gains TestALoudStepReportsItsTailNotItsHead and provider_claude_test.go gains TestTimeoutDiagnosticIsTheBoundedTailOfStderr; no existing assertion is deleted, loosened, or made unreachable. Existing asserted texts survive: cellwork's `"git %s produced more than %d bytes"` and `"git " + ... + ": " + msg` are byte-identical, cellcog's `"%s failed: %w (stderr: %s)"` and `"did not finish within ... captured %d stdout bytes before the stall; stderr tail: %q"` are unchanged, and cellcheck's truncation marker text `"...[truncated]...\n"` is preserved as cellbound.Marker. One real behaviour difference exists outside any assertion: cellcog's old tail prefixed a truncated stderr diagnostic with `"…"` while cellbound.Tail prefixes Marker, and cellbound.Tail TrimSpaces cellcheck step tails that the old cellcheck tail did not. Neither text is asserted by any test in the view (TestTimeoutCarriesDiagnostics uses a sub-bound stderr; cellcheck tests use strings.Contains), so AC2 as written is met.

assessment.reason: Both policies have tests that assert WHICH bytes survive, not merely that truncation occurred, and each fails under substitution of the other. TestKeepHeadKeepsTheFirstBytes writes "abcde"+"fghij" to a bound of 4 and requires String() == "abcd"; under KeepTail the same input yields "ghij" and the test fails. TestKeepTailKeepsTheLastBytes is the exact mirror, requiring "ghij"; under KeepHead it yields "abcd" and fails. Caller-level tests reinforce this at the seams: TestALoudStepReportsItsTailNotItsHead requires the tail to contain "the failure at the end" and NOT contain "OPENING-NOISE", and TestTimeoutDiagnosticIsTheBoundedTailOfStderr requires "STALLED-HERE" present and "OPENING-CHATTER" absent — each with a negative assertion, so substituting the opposite policy fails them rather than merely passing vacuously.
